extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instruction conflicts, evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect conflicting commands across 8 tasks.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
extraction.citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., & Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2 [cs.AI].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using AutoCreate, a novel automatic dataset creation framework leveraging programs and large language models. It starts from manually input seeds and automatically generates data through a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline, with human experts double-checking quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is generated from manually input seeds and, for SemanticConflict, from the ImageNet dataset. OCR images are generated with varying font, size, and color.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. For SemanticConflict, the correct label in questions is substituted with similar but different objects. For GeometricConflict, a phrase describing an object is modified to refer to a non-existent object.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner component removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. Three levels of splits are manually selected: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually checked the quality of the generated dataset and provided three levels of splits. LLMs were also used as evaluation agents to assess whether replies successfully identify conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: LLM evaluation agents were validated against human experts using Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate. GPT-4 demonstrated close alignment to human evaluative standards (Spearman's ρ up to 0.999, concordance up to 99%).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as evaluation agent to determine whether replies successfully identify conflicts)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction. It promotes inclusivity in AI research and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only language-language and vision-language paradigms are included; more modalities will be added. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. No detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) for their ability to detect self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms.

name.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands.

description.evidence: It encompasses 20K conflicting instructions and 8 tasks, evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Our work on the SCI benchmark, along with the AutoCreate framework and CaP approach, has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: To begin with, we only include language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in our SCI benchmark based on our automatic framework, AutoCreate. Besides, no fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. Finally, we do not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We propose a multimodal benchmark, Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI), to evaluate the ability of LMMs to detect conflicted instructions.
